key_insight: tttLRM introduces a Test-Time Training (TTT) layer as a fast-weight memory that compresses many input views into an implicit latent 3D representation, enabling long-context autoregressive reconstruction with linear computational complexity. This latent can be decoded into explicit formats (e.g., Gaussian Splats) for downstream use.
problem_solved: Scales 3D reconstruction to long input contexts and many observations without quadratic compute/memory blowup, allowing autoregressive generation from large image sets.
method: Add a Test-Time Training (TTT) layer whose fast weights are produced from multiple image observations, forming a compressed implicit 3D latent.
Perform autoregressive decoding in the latent/fast-weight space with linear computational complexity w.r.t. context length.
Render or convert the implicit latent into explicit representations (e.g., Gaussian Splats) for downstream consumption and evaluation.
impact: Makes large-context, high-capacity 3D reconstruction practical by reducing compute and memory costs, enabling practitioners to process many views and deploy autoregressive 3D models more efficiently and flexibly.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multiple input images → TTT fast-weight encoder → autoregressive latent decoder → explicit outputs (Gaussian Splats).
Complexity plot comparing linear scaling (tttLRM) vs. quadratic or worse scaling of prior methods as number of views increases.
Illustration of fast-weight compression: many images summarized into a compact TTT layer (iconography showing compression/memory).
Before/after or side-by-side reconstruction gallery showing decoded Gaussian Splat outputs and fidelity across varying context lengths.
paper_title: tttLRM: Test-Time Training for Long Context and Autoregressive 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Chen Wang, Hao Tan, Wang Yifan, Zhiqin Chen, Yuheng Liu
